sections.h2: What kind of county is Ballard County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Ballard County sits in the far west of Kentucky, at the confluence of the Ohio and Mississippi rivers, in the region known as the Jackson Purchase. The General Assembly created it on February 15, 1842, from parts of Hickman and McCracken counties. Wickliffe is the county seat, having taken over from Blandville in 1882, and a courthouse fire on February 17, 1880 destroyed most of the early county records.

The county covers about 274 square miles, of which roughly 27 are water, and it belongs to the Paducah, Kentucky and Illinois metropolitan area. Barlow, Kevil, La Center and Wickliffe are its cities. Bandana and Lovelaceville are census-designated places. A single school district, Ballard County Schools, serves the whole county. Axe Lake Swamp State Nature Preserve, a 458-acre wetland in the Barlow Bottoms, is one of its protected areas.

sections.h2: Which Ballard County offices handle your property tax?
sections.html:
Three offices share the work, and all are listed on the county's elected officials page. The Ballard County Sheriff at 437 Ohio Street in Wickliffe collects the bills, with phones at (270) 335-3561 or (270) 335-5153. The Property Valuation Administrator, at 132 North 4th Street, Wickliffe, sets values and takes exemption applications at (270) 335-3400. The County Clerk, in the courthouse at the same 132 North 4th Street address, takes assessment appeals and later holds unpaid bills. Its number is (270) 335-5168.

Call the sheriff for the current bill amount, since the state schedule below sets the dates but each bill carries its own rates.

sections.h2: When are Ballard County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Kentucky sets one regular schedule for every county (KRS 134.015), and Ballard County bills follow it unless the Department of Revenue approves a delayed one. Taxes are due by December 31 of the assessment year, and anyone paying in full by November 1 takes a 2 percent discount. Payment from November 2 through December 31 is at face value. A 5 percent penalty applies in January, and 10 percent applies after January 31.

Bills that remain unpaid after April 15 go to the County Clerk as certificates of delinquency, and a lien is recorded. The Department of Revenue says interest then runs at 1 percent per month, with a county clerk fee, and a county attorney fee once notices go out. Ask the sheriff's office for the dates printed on this year's bill, because a delayed schedule changes each stage to a month-long window.

sections.h2: What is the yearly property tax calendar for a Ballard County owner?
sections.html:
Kentucky property tax calendar that applies to Ballard County owners (Department of Revenue)
StepTiming
Assessment dateJanuary 1
Real property listing periodJanuary 1 to March 1
Personal property listingJanuary 1 to May 15
Public inspection of the tax roll13 days starting the first Monday in May
Appeal filed with clerkBy close of business the day after inspection ends
Local board of assessment appealsMeets 25 to 35 days after inspection, up to five days
Bills mailed and dueDue by December 31

An owner need not list real property again if last year's roll described it fully and correctly and nothing significant changed. A home bought in the prior year can carry the deed value as its listed value for the next January 1.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Ballard County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the PVA at 132 North 4th Street. State law requires a conference with the PVA or a deputy before any appeal. If you meet during the inspection period, you have until the close of business on the following workday to file at the County Clerk, and the appeal form asks for your own opinion of value. That opinion is used for the bill if it is prepared before the appeal ends.

  • Bring evidence: building and land descriptions, insurance policies, construction cost and sales listings.
  • A paid representative must have a recognized professional status and written authority from you.
  • You may audio-record the board hearing.
  • A higher final value brings a supplemental bill for the difference.

The Department of Revenue also notes that an owner who files no appeal, or files and then skips the hearing, cannot continue the appeal to a later stage.

sections.h2: Does Ballard County offer a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Yes, to homeowners who are at least 65 or are classified as totally disabled. The application goes to the Ballard County PVA, which holds the property records. The state exemption is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, subtracted from the assessed value, and it changes every two years.

That matters in a county where the Census survey shows 23.3 percent of residents are 65 or older,. Ballard's population was 7,594 in 2025, down 1.8 percent from the April 2020 base, so a large share of owners are retirees who may qualify and have never applied.

sections.h2: What do Ballard County home values mean for a seller?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 survey puts the median value of an owner-occupied home in Ballard County at $145,800. About 76 percent of the 3,209 households own their home, the median household income is $66,164, and median gross rent is $817. The county has 3,730 housing units and a land area of about 247 square miles, so there is roughly 31 people per square mile.

With values in that range, a property tax bill is a modest line at closing, but an unpaid year or two can grow quickly because of the penalties and fees above. A seller who inherited a river-county house, or who moved away, should ask the sheriff for every unpaid year before the deed is signed.

  • Request a payoff for current and prior bills.
  • Ask the clerk whether a delinquency lien is recorded.
  • Put a mailing address for the next bill into the deed.

sections.h2: Who pays the property tax when a Ballard County house sells?
sections.html:
Kentucky treats the tax as a personal debt of the owner on the assessment date, and a recorded delinquency lien follows the property for up to eleven years whoever owns it. In practice the closing agent collects the year's bill from the seller's proceeds, often prorated, and sends it to the sheriff. Ask the closing agent how the year's bill will be split between you and the buyer.

Owners who want to sell fast, with taxes behind, can ask for a written cash offer on the house as it is. The buyer's closing agent deducts any lien balance from the proceeds, so the seller does not have to pay the sheriff first.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Ballard County?
faqs.a: The Ballard County Sheriff does, from 437 Ohio Street in Wickliffe. The phone numbers listed on the county's elected officials page are (270) 335-3561 and (270) 335-5153.

faqs.q: What discount do I get for paying early in Ballard County?
faqs.a: A 2 percent discount applies if the bill is paid in full by November 1. KRS 134.015 sets that rule, and the face amount is due from November 2 through December 31.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the December 31 deadline?
faqs.a: A 5 percent penalty applies for January, and 10 percent applies after January 31. Unpaid bills move to the County Clerk after April 15 and begin to collect interest at 1 percent per month.

faqs.q: Where do I file an assessment appeal?
faqs.a: File it at the Ballard County Clerk's office, 132 North 4th Street, after a conference with the PVA. The deadline is the close of business on the workday after the inspection period ends.

faqs.q: Does Ballard County have its own homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The exemption is a Kentucky program, not a county one. Apply to the Ballard County PVA at (270) 335-3400 if you are 65 or older or totally disabled. The 2025 and 2026 amount is $49,100.
